overview: After 1.e4 Nf6 2.e5 Nd5 White plays 3.Na3, an unusual developing move that hopes for c4 or Nc4. Black has a free hand with ...d6, ...c5 or ...e6 and challenges the e5 pawn. White does not get a clear advantage and the knight on a3 is awkward.

white_ideas.idea: Bring the knight to c4 and play c4 or d4
Keep e5 supported with d4 and f4

typical_structures.structure: White e5 pawn against Black fianchetto or d6 pawn structures

character.notes: Quiet and manoeuvring; neither side forces matters early.

soundness.notes: Safe but gives White no edge.

structure.notes: The centre can transform and is not fixed.

character.reason: It is neither sharp nor especially solid, just an unusual quiet line.

soundness.reason: A harmless but playable side line.

level.reason: Plans are about the centre and space.

plans.reason: White grabs space with e5 while Black attacks the advanced centre with pieces.
